s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic hematochezia in an immunocompromised patient with gastrointestinal polyps and mixed inflammatory infiltrate
salient_findings: Multiple semisessile polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon
Mixed inflammatory infiltrate with pale histiocytes and eosinophils
Basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes
key_facts: 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
Receiving maintenance therapy with 6-mercaptopurine, methotrexate, vincristine, and dexamethasone
Intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
Denies abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
Stool studies negative for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus
Colonoscopy showed multiple polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon
Histologic examination revealed eroded surface mucosa and reactive hyperplastic glands
Lamina propria expanded by dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate
Histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions
Inclusions were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains
Fungal and acid-fast stains were negative for organisms

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus-associated hematochezia
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with gastrointestinal symptoms and mixed inflammatory infiltrate

shortlist.label: Neutropenic colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is intermittently neutropenic and has gastrointestinal symptoms

shortlist.label: Graft-versus-host disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of immunocompromise and gastrointestinal symptoms

shortlist.label: Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic examination revealed histiocytes with basophilic inclusions

shortlist.label: Malacoplakia
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic examination revealed eroded surface mucosa and mixed inflammatory infiltrate

raw.rationale: The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that are strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains is characteristic of Malacoplakia, a rare inflammatory condition often associated with immunocompromised states.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus-associated hematochezia
rejected.why: Stool studies and histologic examination did not reveal evidence of cytomegalovirus infection.

rejected.label: Neutropenic colitis
rejected.why: While the patient is intermittently neutropenic, the colonoscopy and histologic findings do not support a diagnosis of neutropenic colitis, which typically presents with more severe inflammation and necrosis.

rejected.label: Graft-versus-host disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of a recent transplant or other risk factors for graft-versus-host disease, and the histologic findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Histiocytosis
rejected.why: The histologic findings of eroded surface mucosa, reactive hyperplastic glands, and a dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate are not typical of histiocytosis, which usually presents with a more uniform proliferation of histiocytes.
